builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: 3DCodeEdit: Benchmarking Instruction-Guided 3D Program Editing
summary: The paper contributes a benchmark, but its actionable technique replaces single-shot generation of 3D code edits with a multi-turn loop where a separate reviewer model compares renders against the request and feeds discrepancies back to the editor. It costs extra inference rounds: each attempt requires rendering plus a reviewer-model call, multiplying latency and API spend per edit. It can fail because reviewer feedback only partially compensates for missing geometric foresight, and it depends on a reviewer able to perceive render discrepancies accurately, which itself degrades on subtle structural or style errors.
rationale: The render-and-review feedback loop is implementable with API models and no training, but its benefit is demonstrated only on Blender 3D code editing and must be validated on the reader's own workload before adoption.

claims.statement: The paper contributes a benchmark, but its actionable technique replaces single-shot generation of 3D code edits with a multi-turn loop where a separate reviewer model compares renders against the request and feeds discrepancies back to the editor. It costs extra inference rounds: each attempt requires rendering plus a reviewer-model call, multiplying latency and API spend per edit. It can fail because reviewer feedback only partially compensates for missing geometric foresight, and it depends on a reviewer able to perceive render discrepancies accurately, which itself degrades on subtle structural or style errors.

Average success across 17 models is 37%; reviewer-model render feedback raises a 27B model above the single-shot rate of a 2.8T-parameter model, and beats maximum reasoning effort or an agent harness.
